steps.title: Define a FeatureFlag type with string literal union
steps.instruction: Create a type called FeatureFlag that is a union of string literals representing valid feature flag names. Use 'newDashboard', 'darkMode', and 'aiAssistant' as the possible values.
steps.hint: In TypeScript, you can define a union type using the pipe (|) symbol between string literal values.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: A union type for theme options
type Theme = 'light' | 'dark' | 'auto';

steps.title: Create a FeatureFlagConfig interface
steps.instruction: Create an interface named FeatureFlagConfig with a property 'key' of type FeatureFlag and a property 'enabled' of type boolean.
steps.hint: Define an interface with typed properties using the FeatureFlag type you created earlier.
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have a FeatureFlagConfig interface with typed properties for key and enabled.
successCriteria: The FeatureFlagConfig interface is defined with 'key: FeatureFlag' and 'enabled: boolean' properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the FeatureFlagConfig interface with properly typed properties.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure your interface has both 'key' and 'enabled' properties with the correct types.
steps.feedbackWrong: The interface definition doesn't match the requirements. Check that you've included both properties with the specified types.

steps.title: Define a FeatureFlagVariant type with discriminated union
steps.instruction: Define a new type named FeatureFlagVariant that uses a discriminated union to represent different variant types.
steps.hint: Create a type that uses union syntax (|) between different object types, each with a common discriminant property (like 'type').
steps.expectedOutcome: A FeatureFlagVariant type is defined using discriminated union syntax with at least two variant types.
successCriteria: FeatureFlagVariant type is defined with union syntax and includes discriminant properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully defined a discriminated union type for feature flag variants.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure your type uses union syntax (|) and includes discriminant properties.
steps.feedbackWrong: The FeatureFlagVariant type definition is missing or incorrect. Try creating a discriminated union type.

steps.title: Create a FeatureFlagState interface
steps.instruction: Create an interface named FeatureFlagState to manage the state of feature flags. It should have a property named flags that is a Record mapping FeatureFlag keys to boolean values.
steps.hint: Define an interface with the correct name and a property that uses the Record utility type.
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have a FeatureFlagState interface ready to track which feature flags are enabled or disabled.
successCriteria: An interface named FeatureFlagState is defined with a flags property of type Record<FeatureFlag, boolean>.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the FeatureFlagState interface. This will be the foundation for managing flag states.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure your interface is named FeatureFlagState and includes a flags property with the correct Record type.
steps.feedbackWrong: The interface isn't quite correct. Check that you've named it FeatureFlagState and defined a flags property with the proper type.

steps.instruction: Create a constant named 'featureFlagConfig' that uses the FeatureFlagConfig interface to define a configuration object for a 'darkMode' feature flag.
steps.hint: Use the 'const' keyword to declare a variable. Assign it an object with the required properties from the FeatureFlagConfig interface.
steps.expectedOutcome: A typed configuration object is created with the correct structure for a feature flag.
successCriteria: The 'featureFlagConfig' constant is declared with the FeatureFlagConfig type and includes the required properties for a feature flag.

steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure your object includes all required properties from the FeatureFlagConfig interface.

steps.instruction: Create a function named getFeatureVariant that returns a FeatureFlagVariant type based on the feature flag name and configuration.
steps.hint: The function should take a feature flag name (string) and the configuration object as parameters, then return the appropriate variant from the configuration.
steps.expectedOutcome: A getFeatureVariant function that returns typed feature flag variants from the configuration.
successCriteria: The getFeatureVariant function is defined with proper TypeScript types and returns a FeatureFlagVariant.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully implemented the getFeatureVariant function with proper typing.

steps.instruction: Create a FeatureFlagManager class with a constructor that takes a FeatureFlagConfig parameter and stores it as a private property.

steps.expectedOutcome: A FeatureFlagManager class with a typed constructor and private config property is created.
